title: The Fragmentation
sub: Your budget is not underperforming. It is leaking, in three places you can name and price.

title: Where the money actually goes

callouts.head: Repeat questions
callouts.body: The same answer, re-derived weekly, by four people who never meet.

callouts.head: Version confusion
callouts.body: Two live sources, both plausible, neither owned.

callouts.head: Onboarding drag
callouts.body: Every new hire rebuilds context that already existed.

verdict: Recoverable waste is structural, not behavioural.
sub: You cannot train your way out of a missing system.

title: Two ways to run the same account
verdict: Same spend. Different system. Different outcome.

tiers.head: Auto-correct
tiers.body: The system resolves it silently. Nobody is notified.

tiers.head: Bot-assisted
tiers.body: Action taken, human override offered in the same card.

tiers.head: Executive escalation
tiers.body: P1 faults or 30-day unresolved issues. Two-hour SLA.

title: What the change is worth

cells.label: Year 1 investment
cells.body: No incremental software cost. Admin, team lead and project lead hours.

cells.label: Base case return
cells.body: Driven by a 50 percent reduction in repeat questions and version confusion.

cells.label: Payback
cells.body: Year one ROI of 16x to 25x on the base case.

verdict: State it as a range. Defend the low end.
sub: The base case survives a 60 percent haircut and still pays back inside a quarter.

callouts.head: Compounding
callouts.body: Each turn makes the next one cheaper.

callouts.head: Governed
callouts.body: Every stage has an owner and a cadence.

callouts.head: Instrumented
callouts.body: If it moves, it is measured.

title: One decision, this week

options.head: Do nothing
rows: Every hire pays the same tax
The gap is invisible until it is expensive

options.head: Commit
rows: Kill switch on day 31 if it fails

verdict: The only expensive option is the one that stays invisible.
